A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same vec2vec research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original embedding-translation, attribute-inference, and inversion experiments, alongside component and training-data ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen translation, MS COCO retrieval, initialization-robustness, and TweetTopic inversion results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 substantially changes the stated VSP objective: v3 preserves each batch's inner products through its own translation, whereas v4 compares them with translated inner products from the opposite batch. Normalization also changes from 1/B to 1/B². This redefines a key training constraint; the architecture and other losses remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v4 adds actual caption-to-image retrieval on MS COCO, extending evaluation beyond the text-only inputs used with CLIP in v3. It also extends inversion evaluation from Enron emails to tweets. The original NQ, TweetTopic, MIMIC, and Enron coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 9 introduces direct CLIP text-image retrieval as a comparator to translated Granite queries. Appendix B also newly specifies evaluating both entropic and non-entropic Gromov-Wasserstein variants. The existing naïve, oracle, and optimal-transport comparator families remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include Qwen-GTE evaluation with 1,024-candidate ranking batches, MS COCO evaluation over 5,000 images using Recall@16, a fixed ten-epoch initialization study, and inversion on 50 tweets. These materially expand the evaluation design. Existing main translation experiments retain their stated 8,192-candidate batches and training-data setup.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a substantive test of training reliability across initializations and backbone relationships: 14/15 e5-to-gte runs reach 80% top-1 accuracy, versus 3/15 e5-to-gtr runs. This directly characterizes a previously unquantified failure condition. The component and data-size ablations from v3 Appendix D are retained in v4 Section 7.

E5.justification: v4 newly reports fifteen random initializations per model pair and convergence frequencies for the dedicated robustness study. v3 only states that the best of multiple initializations is selected. Existing tables retain their standard-error reporting; the new study does not establish increased repetition of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Revised OT results include Table 2's selected GTE-to-GTR baseline rank changing from 4078.45 to 3064.16, while vec2vec remains 2.64. In Table 4, GTE-to-CLIP OT cosine changes from 0.59 to 0.76, overtaking the retained vec2vec value of 0.62. New results include GTE-to-Qwen top-1 accuracy of 0.92, COCO Recall@16 of 0.23 versus CLIP's 0.75, and tweet leakage reaching 67%. These include revised baseline evaluations and new settings, rather than improved existing vec2vec scores.

T1.justification: The VSP mathematical definition in Section 3.2 changes both its normalization and the inner-product terms being equated; this is not equivalent notation. The Strong Platonic Representation Hypothesis, other formal objectives, and evaluation definitions remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction raises the claimed maximum target-space cosine similarity from 0.92 to 0.96. Section 5 and Table 2 still report a maximum of 0.92, so the stronger numerical claim is not corroborated there. The abstract, central novelty claim, and security implications otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v4 adds backbone-dependent initialization reliability as a concrete limitation. Appendix C limits Qwen conclusions to one expensive model pair and hypothesizes a model-performance gap behind its reverse-direction cosine shortfall. Appendix D interprets COCO results as enabling modality transfer without multimodal training.

D1.justification: Appendix A revises the accounting from 45 trained models and approximately 180 GPU days to 25 fully trained plus 30 partially trained models and approximately 176 GPU days. It adds the Qwen run's twenty-day A100 cost, while Table 1 adds Qwen specifications. These are revised disclosures, not demonstrated efficiency gains. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for Microsoft COCO and Qwen3 Embedding. Existing cited works and the substantive positioning against representation alignment, optimal transport, inversion, and modality-bridging research are retained.

P1.justification: The existing appendix ablations become main-text Section 7, shifting related work and discussion to Sections 8 and 9. Appendices are reorganized around the added evaluations, with localized prose edits, updated conference text, and an additional funding acknowledgment. Most existing exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Qwen and COCO result tables and a TweetTopic inversion heatmap, plus a Qwen row in Table 1. Existing ablation tables move into the main text, and other tables and the judge-prompt figure are renumbered and repositioned. The original explanatory figures and heatmaps are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 improves empirical scrutiny through quantified initialization failures, expanded OT evaluation, and actual image-retrieval evidence. However, the non-equivalent VSP revision is not reconciled with the retained vec2vec results, and the new 0.96 introductory claim lacks support in the translation tables. The PDFs do not resolve whether the loss revision corrects documentation or changes the evaluated method. This uncertainty about a central methodological change prevents a reliable net quality judgment despite the useful empirical additions.
